thread:
Alex Chen: Hey team — heads up, we need a GCP quota + project approval for a staged canary.

Details: need 16 x H100 (a100 replacement path) in europe-west1 for inference-prod-canary project and 4 x TPU v4 cores in us-central1 for eval/throughput tests. Target window: next Tuesday (7 days). Also need compute.googleapis.com enabled on the project, svc account whitelisted, and Shared VPC peering from host-network project. No external IPs.

Priya Patel: @Alex can you paste project ID + billing account? Also need a short cost justification for finance.

Alex Chen: Project: inference-prod-canary (project id: redwood-inference-canary-eu, project number: 987654321012). Billing account: BA0A-XXXX-YYYY.
Cost sketch: H100 on-demand approx $30/hr -> 16 * $30 * 24 * 7 = ~$80k for the week. TPU v4 around $8/hr/core -> 4 * $8 * 24 * 7 = ~$5.4k. Total ~ $86k. We will only run for 48 hours at full capacity per stage; rest of time is lower.

Mateo Ruiz: Are org policies blocking H100 in europe-west1? Last time we had a folder-level restriction on new GPU types. Also need the service-account redwood-canary@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com added to the Shared VPC host project.

Alex Chen: Good call. I checked earlier: there is a constraint at org level for compute.trustedImageProjects but not gpu-specific denies. I still filed an org-policy exception request in the console.

Alex Chen: Here's the gcloud snippet I used to check quotas:
```
gcloud compute regions describe europe-west1 --project=redwood-inference-canary-eu --format=json | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS_PER_PROJECT")'
```
It returned current usage 0 and limit 8 for H100 family. Need 16 -> request increase to 24 to allow headroom.

Erin ONeill: @Alex please include a short runbook for rollback if things go sideways (e.g., fallback to L4 family or lower model batch size). Also security wants to confirm no external IPs and KMS key usage for disk encryption.

Alex Chen: Runbook (brief):
- Step 1: Start canary with 4 H100s, validate latency + correctness against eval set.
- Step 2: If QPS or latency exceed SLO, scale down to 2 H100 and switch to L4-quantized model.
- Step 3: If model quality regression, abort canary and route traffic to baseline model in dedicated cluster.
KMS key: projects/redwood-keys/locations/global/keyRings/inference/cryptoKeys/canary-key. No external IPs, using internal NL7 LB.

Samir Kapur: For the quota request, we need the CRO contact and an explicit business justification line for GCP. Can you add one-liner: "Short-term validation for production rollout of new 32k LLM serving on H100s; expected to reduce token cost by 40% vs current setup". Also cc cost-ops.

Alex Chen: Added justification text to support case. I just submitted the support request:
- Case ID: 12345678901234
- Type: Quota increase (GPUs/H100) + TPU quota
- Link: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/12345678901234?project=redwood-inference-canary-eu

infra-bot: Quota request submitted on behalf of Alex Chen. Estimated GCP response time: 48-72 hours. Ticket 12345678901234.

Priya Patel: approving from product side. @Mateo can infra expedite if org-policy exception needed?

Mateo Ruiz: I'll ping the infra admin and org-policy lead. Please add me as an approver on the support case.

Alex Chen: Done — Mateo is added. Also added security (Erin) and cost-ops.

infra-bot: Update: GCP support replied requesting project owner confirmation and billing contact. Action required by project owner to reply with billing confirmation.

Alex Chen: Replied to support with billing confirmation and attached the brief cost justification.

infra-bot: Final update: Quota increase partially approved. H100 quota in europe-west1 increased to 20 (request 24, approved 20). TPU v4 quota in us-central1 approved as requested (4 cores). Case closed.

Priya Patel: Nice. Adjust runbook to use 20 H100 max; we can stagger canaries. :tada:

Samir Kapur: Tagging cost-ops to monitor actual spend during the run: @cost-ops.

Alex Chen: Thanks all — starting staged rollout next Tue. I'll post a short postmortem after the canary.
